In a press conference earlier today, held by Chinese National Space Administration leader [Xu Dazhe](http://www.apsco.int/apsco-ad/imapic/20151141574141173.jpg), he announced a new project that the CNSA was working on. The transcript and links were uploaded on the official website for those who did not tune in to read about.

"With humanity on the verge of another era, the Interplanetary Era, work must be done in the remaining time to make sure the era comes to fruition.

The biggest space project developed by humanity, the International Space Station, contains a volume of 106 m3. Yet if humanity is to advance, expansion is a must. Taking inspiration from NASA's [B330](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B330), CNSA is developing their own version of the B330.

Dubbed the C11037, the C11307 will have improved radiation protection compared to the B330 and ISS. The walls will made up of ballistic, thermal, and radiation protection, giving a strength exceeding concrete when fully completed. The thickness of the walls will be at .5 meters. After fully inflated, 8 UV resistant windows will be able to be viewed out of, into the vastness of space.

Surrounding the C11037 will be [Perovskite Solar Cells](https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/energy-environment/wp/2016/01/15/this-technology-may-be-the-future-of-solar-energy/), which their "efficiency levels comparable to those of commercially used silicon cells — upwards of 20 percent." On the connecting module will be traditional solar arrays, seen throughout every spacecraft.

Another improvement over the B330 will be increased space. Currently, the B330 sits at 13.7 meters (45 feet) long by 6.7 meters (22 feet) in diameter. CNSA is planning to expand that by half, and have the C11037 be 20.55 meters (67.5 feet) long by 10.05 meters (33 feet) in diameter. With that room, more astronauts and equipment will be able to be on board the space habitat, compared to the B330. To give insight onto this, it is expected to hold a total of 12 people, and improvement over the ISS's 7 maximum. In order to support this new room in the event of lower pressure, foldable steel alloy beams will be installed on the ends and in the center to keep the habitat big enough for inhabitants to exit. Yet this comes with a drawback, of an increased weight of 30,000 kg (66000 lbs).

In all, this project is expected to take a total of 3 years, as it is just improving a structure that already exists. As for cost, it is expected to cost around $1 billion USD to engineer a create a perfect version. Constructing others will cost around $250 million after the first one is created.

The CNSA would love to work with other nations on the project, especially Russia and America, yet due to current legal issues classifying China as a threat to America, that is not possible, even if it is to benefit the future of humanity.

As for other nations, it is expected to have 3 seats be available for other nations to buy for a ride. The other nine seats will be reserved for two American, two Russian, and five Chinese astronauts. At this time, prices are undecided, but CNSA is willing to let nations reserve seats."
